answers.explanation: A Wi-Fi driver author doesn't think about web pages, and a browser author doesn't think about radio.
A router reads the network-layer header (the destination IP address) and treats everything after it as opaque data.
That's what keeps the layers independent of each other.
Swappable layers are how the Internet achieves network technology independence.
Tunneling is how VPNs work: your traffic is wrapped in an encrypted outer packet addressed to the VPN server.
Each layer only looks at its own header, so traffic hidden inside an allowed protocol looks allowed. That's why tunneling is a security issue.
Splitting and rebuilding are invisible to the application, unless it works at the session layer and manages that itself.
